title: Drone delivery of blood to health facilities in Rwanda (Zipline, from 2016) and its measured effects

facts.text: Blood products have a short shelf life, and demand at individual hospitals goes up and down, which makes them hard to supply.
Before drones, patients in rural Rwanda who needed blood had to wait for shipments from Kigali, which could take a long time and could spoil on the way.
Away from Rwanda's main paved roads, routes are mostly dirt, and the long rainy season makes travel slower.
In 2016 the Rwandan government and Zipline, a company based in the United States, started delivering medical supplies by drone from a base in Muhanga District.
Zipline's drones, called Zips, are small battery-powered fixed-wing planes without wheels, launched from a catapult-like launcher.
A Zip can fly round trips of up to 150 kilometers and carry up to 1.5 kilograms of supplies.
Health workers order supplies by text message.
A Zip does not land; it drops a box on a paper parachute near the health facility and flies back to base.
A 2022 study in The Lancet Global Health examined blood deliveries to 20 health facilities in Rwanda.
Between March 2017 and December 2019, drones delivered 12,733 blood product orders to these facilities, and 43 percent of them were emergency orders.
The average drone delivery took 49.6 minutes, 79 minutes faster than estimated delivery by road.
The time saved ranged from 3 to 211 minutes, depending on the distance to the facility and the quality of the roads.
After drone deliveries began, the number of blood units that expired fell, a 67 percent reduction after 12 months.
The study's authors said future research should check whether drone delivery is cost-effective.
On-demand deliveries have helped Rwanda's national blood service reduce waste and shortages.
Zips depend on mobile phone networks, which need base stations along every flight route and a constant power supply.
Before Zipline, blood deliveries to some hospitals took at least three hours.

notes: Zipline 的啟用月份各報導不一（Smithsonian 2016 年 10 月啟用；TIME 寫第一次送血是 2016 年 12 月 21 日），選文只寫 2016 年。「15 分鐘送達」是個別醫院的說法，選文不用；平均時間一律用 Lancet Global Health 研究的 49.6 分鐘。
